caption: The drawing depicts a single, ornately designed teapot rendered in shades of grey and black, suggesting the use of pencil or graphite on paper. The teapot is elongated horizontally, with a large, rounded body that rests on three spherical feet. The spout is long and curves gently upward, extending to the right side of the image, while the handle, located on the left, is thick, angular, and shaded more darkly than other parts of the drawing, possibly indicating a different material or a shadow effect. The teapot has a fitted lid with a small knob on top. Inscribed on the body of the teapot, there is text in different font styles and sizes, some of which is written in italics. The inscription starts with "STATE OF NEW-YORK" and mentions the award of a premium to Nicholas Smith of Saratoga for the second-best specimen of woolen cloth in 1813. The drawing is bordered by a single rectangular outline, and there is a small linear scale labeled "scale" at the bottom right corner. The overall composition centers the teapot with minimal background detail or additional objects present.
title: Silver Teapot
